newsitem.title: UK: Singapore/UK air traffic talks seen early February.
newsitem.headline: Singapore/UK air traffic talks seen early February.

text.p: LONDON (Reuter) Jan 16 - A third round of talks on air traffic rights between the United Kingdom and Singapore is expected to take place in the island state in early to mid-February, a Singapore Airlines spokesman said.
"The two governments are in the process of negotiating new services for UK and Singapore airlines to the two countries and beyond," he told Reuters.
"It could virtually provide open skies with unlimited access to Britain and Singapore for the airlines involved."
Earlier talks were held in March and July 1996 with a third round due last December, but postponed at the request of the UK authorities.

At present SIA has two daily Boeing 747 flights into London-Heathrow and it is seeking to add a third. It also flies three times a week to Manchester -- which will increase to four this April-- and it would like this service to offer daily flights within two to three years, he added.
British Airways Plc flies 11 times a week to Singapore and rights exist, but have not been taken up for more flights by UK scheduled carriers.
With all services between the two countries reciprocal, UK carriers would enjoy exactly the same rights as SIA under a new liberal framework, industry sources noted.
At present, SIA has a twice weekly 747-400 freighter service into London-Heathrow and is seeking "some increase in cargo capacity" during the negotiations, the spokesman said.
Singapore is also looking for one of its flights to Heathrow under the new agreement to be extended to provide a daily transatlantic service to New York, he added.
This has been an outstanding request for some time and even if granted by the UK it would still need a go-ahead for landing rights from the U.S authorities.
SIA's proposed transatlantic service could supply some additional if limited competition on the route.

At present, only three non-U.S. or non-UK carriers operate between London and the United States. These are Air India with daily flights, El Al, which flies three times a week as does Kuwait Airlines, industry sources said.

The UK-Singapore talks are not linked to the bilateral talks talks between the UK and U.S. However, there is an apparent reluctance by the UK to consider Singapore's request for transatlantic rights until the UK-U.S. talks are finalised, the sources added.
